claims.statement: Email-header reference declares FPT/GHEC/GHES and describes client filtering/forwarding capability, not authorization to forward private notifications or install mail rules.

Expected From is notifications@github.com for FPT, github.com or subdomain.ghe.com for GHEC and administrator-configured no-reply for GHES. Header value alone is not authenticated sender evidence; tenant/platform identity must remain explicit.

X-GitHub-Recipient and Recipient-Address identify intended recipient when mail appears misdirected; email setup may deliver another user's notifications. Receipt by inbox owner does not grant underlying access/disclosure authority.

To identifies thread reply endpoint; replying adds conversation comment. Reply is external write needing exact thread/recipient and authority checks, not a passive acknowledgment or read-only operation.

Cc includes subscriber and reason address with product-specific suffix. Reasons include assign/author/ci_activity/comment/manual/mention/push/review_requested/security_alert/state_change/subscribed/team_mention/your_activity; email underscore vocabulary differs inbox hyphen grammar.

CI-activity reason specifically describes triggered workflow completion, not success or required-check acceptance. Security/review/state reasons are event routing signals, not current evaluated control outcomes.
List-Id prose format OWNER/REPOSITORY <REPOSITORY.OWNER> differs example's product-url suffix; preserve ambiguity and actual parser fixtures instead of inventing exact normalized identity from prose.

Severity fragment describes severity for Dependabot alerts and low/moderate/high/critical levels; header severity is source classification, not risk acceptance, actual remediation or complete vulnerability inventory.
No real personal mail inspected/forwarded, reply sent or filter installed. Actual delivery/authentication/privacy and current target coverage remain independently verified work.
